summary: ```# Marvelous Designer 2024.1: Feature Overview ## AI Texture Generator With the **AI Texture Generator**, you can easily type in keywords to generate different texture images to choose from to create new fabric textures. 1. **Select Fabric**: Choose a fabric in the Fabric window. 2. **Access Fabric Properties**: Under the Fabric Properties, Materials, click the **AI Generator** button on the right side of the basic parameters. 3. **Choose Fabric Type**: Select the desired fabric type. 4. **Select Content Type**: Under Content Type, select the type of texture image you want to generate. 5. **Enter Text Prompt**: Input the text prompt. Listing the desired words, rather than a long descriptive sentence, can generate more effective results. 6. **Generate Image**: Click the **Generate** button and check the generated image in the Preview window. **Note**: At the release of 2024.1, prompts can only be entered in the English language. The generated image is stored in the History. The generated images will remain in Preview until you click the **Apply** button. You can click **Generate** again to create more images. Previously generated images with prompts are recorded as Histories, which remain accessible until Marvelous Designer is closed. ## AI Graphic Generator The **AI Graphic Generator** functions similarly to the AI Texture Generator. 1. **Generate Graphics**: You can type in keywords to generate different graphic images to choose from to create new graphics. 2. **Add Graphics to Patterns**: Add any graphic image to a pattern using the **Add Graphic 2D Pattern** tool. 3. **Access Graphic Properties**: Under the Graphic Properties, click the **AI Graphic Generator** button to the right of the basic parameters. Here you can set the Content Type, Transparent Background, and Endpoint. 4. **Generate Graphic**: Once you've set the parameters, click the **Generate** button. The generated graphic is stored in History. To apply the selected image as a graphic, click **Apply**. In the property editor under the graphic configuration, select the desired tile type and use the **Transform Graphic** tool to adjust the transformation, rotation, and scale of the graphic. ## PBR Map Generation **PBR maps** can automatically be generated and applied to graphic images or imported base color texture maps. 1. **Apply Graphic Image**: First, use the **Graphic 2D Pattern** tool to apply a graphic image to the pattern. 2. **Create PBR Map**: Select the graphic using the Edit Texture tool. In the Property Editor, click the **Create PBR Map** button next to the map channels. 3. **Adjust Normal Map**: In this example, the normal map is generated, and you can adjust the intensity for the general normal map in the Property Editor. 4. **Storage of PBR Maps**: The generated PBR map is automatically stored in the App Data Path on your PC. Click on the map thumbnail image to check the save path. **Note**: Create PBR Map support is available for displacement maps, opacity maps, roughness maps, and metalness maps. This feature applies to single models and bump outputs, including fabrics, buttons, trims, graphics, buttonholes, top stitching, and puckering. ## Trim Management You can now manage trim styles in a **Trim Window**. 1. **Load Trim Styles**: To load Trim Styles into the Trim Window, you can import OBJ or FBX files as Trim Types. Click **Add Button** to the Trim Window and add your file, or drag and drop the file into the Trim window. 2. **Apply Trims**: Drag the style from the Trim window to the 3D window to apply and glue. You can select your trims in the 3D window. 3. **Assign Trims**: In the Trim window, click the **Assign** button to replace the trimmed styles onto existing trims. By clicking a trimmed Style in the Trim window, you can change the properties of all assigned trims all at once. 4. **Save/Load Trim Files**: You can easily save and load Trim files with the **Open/Save** button in the Trim Style Property Window. ## USD File Support Cloth simulation and avatar animation can now be exported and imported with **USTFile** format. 1. **Import USD Files**: Go to the main menu, select **File > Import USD**, and select your USTFile. The Imported file appears in your folder for saving or importing trim files. 2. **Import Dialog Box**: The import dialog box is similar to other file types, allowing you to set load and object types. Change the scale preset if necessary. 3. **Axis Conversion**: In Marvelous Designer, the Y-axis is up. Under axis conversion, select the up axis from the application where the file was imported. Marvelous Designer will compare the up axis to the incoming file and apply conversion if necessary. 4. **USD File Import**: Click **OK** and the USD file will be imported. The USD layer window will automatically pop up if it's not already visible in the workspace, allowing you to view the prim path for the imported USD file. **Note**: If the file contains skeletal animation, an animation track is created in the animation window. Create or import garments and record simulation. Cloth simulation can be exported to the existing USD file. Ensure the USD file you are exporting is set to the authoring layer. ## Enhanced 2D Window Features A new viewing option in the **2D window** displays the layer number and color code to help visualize layers. 1. **Activate Layer Display**: Click the **show pattern layer** option under the 2D information icon to activate. If a layer function is applied to pattern pieces, the layer number will be indicated and patterns with the same layer will share the same color. 2. **Layer Color Coding**: Layers 1 through 23 each have a different color value, which repeats from 24 onward. Negative layers are applied in reverse order. 3. **Deactivate Layer Display**: Click the **show pattern layer** option again to deactivate. The layer depth display will automatically turn off when switching to another 2D pattern rendering style. ## Ruler and Guideline Features The 2D pattern ruler display toggle is located under the **2D information** section. 1. **Change Ruler Units**: Right-click on the ruler to change the unit. The ruler will automatically scale when zooming in and out. 2. **Set Ruler Origin**: To change the ruler origin point, click and drag the empty square in the upper left corner of the ruler. When the mouse click is released, the origin point is set to the crosshair position. Double-click or right-click in the empty square to re-initialize the origin point. 3. **Create Guidelines**: Click and drag either the vertical or horizontal ruler to create guidelines. The created guideline will automatically snap to segment points of patterns. 4. **Guideline Options**: Right-click on a guideline to access options such as deleting a guideline, locking guidelines, or creating more guidelines with offsets. ## UV Packing Enhancements The **UV packing algorithm** has been improved to yield better quality results. 1. **Select UV Shells**: Select UV shells and click the **UV packing** button. 2. **Adjust Fidelity Parameter**: A new parameter, fidelity, has been added. The larger the value, the more sensitively the shape of the UV shells is calculated. 3. **Advanced Placement Option**: When advanced placement is turned off, UV shells are placed sequentially from largest to smallest. When turned on, numerous sequences are tested for better placement, minimizing empty space. 4. **Pixel Value Adjustments**: UV padding pixel value can now be adjusted or set to infinite during texture baking. ## State Color Management You can now hide the color of the state applied to patterns and mesh. 1. **Hide State Colors**: If states like freeze, solidify, strengthen, and layer are applied to patterns, you can hide the color display in the 3D window by right-clicking in the empty space in the 3D window. Select **Show and Hide Color of the Selected State**. 2. **Show All States**: In the same right-click menu, select **Show All** to bring the color back to display. This feature also works with selected mesh. ## Hand Pose Functions **Partial pose functions** are added to allow for hand poses. 1. **Import Pose Files**: Hand poses can be applied to the avatar with HPOS files and POS files for Marvelous Designer female version 2 and male version 2 avatars. 2. **Apply Hand Poses**: Import a pose file and in the pop-up window under partial pose, you can select both hands, right or left hand to apply the pose for the hands only. 3. **Simulation Activation**: Simulation is automatically turned on, transitioning the hands from the original pose to the newly applied pose. **Note**: The HPOS file format deals only with hand poses. Hand pose can be applied differently to each hand. If multiple avatars are loaded, you should first select the avatar to apply it to. ```
